title: Unique generator-normalized finite open scalar comparisons
statement: Fix a prime l, a finite extension E of Q_l, an open immersion j:U→X, and supplied Operations o of [def-sf-open-semilinear-tensor-model-data]. There is exactly one IntegralOpenReduction.TensorComparison for o: at each finite coefficient n its natural isomorphism commutes extension by zero with scalar reduction, and on each original extension summand it sends the scalar unit of [x] to the finite extension summand of the scalar unit of x. This is only a family of finite natural isomorphisms; it asserts no strict-system comparison or quotient-transition compatibility.

source.place: Tags 03DI (lemma-extension-by-zero), 03EK (section-tensor-product) and 0E8I (lemma-j-shriek-and-tensor); finite scalar comparison substep of lem-sf-open-strict-scalar-transport.

proof.text: At each finite coefficient n apply the existing semilinear slice scalar generator comparison to the constant tower with value the nth coefficient sheaf and constant algebra map the completed projection. Only its coefficient-linear component at index zero and its generator formula are used.

Apply the proved unit-normalized finite scalar transport to the chosen normalized scalar model on the slice. It supplies the natural isomorphism between scalar extension transported from U and scalar extension on the slice, with its formula on every original scalar unit.

For each source module, identify the recorded ambient scalar-extension object with its actual sheafified tensor object. Compose the generic coefficient-linear component with extension of the inverse slice scalar comparison and the inverse slice tensor object identification. This constructs the finite coefficient-linear isomorphism.

The ambient normalized scalar unit is the image of one tensor the extension summand. The generic generator equation sends this to the extension summand of one tensor the original slice section. The normalized scalar-model unit and the unit equation of the transported adjunction identify its image with the original finite scalar unit. Naturality of the localized extension unit moves the transported scalar comparison through the extension summand. This proves exactly the required generator formula.

Two morphisms out of scalar extension of an open extension are equal when their values on all scalar units of original extension summands agree: apply injectivity of the scalar-adjunction Hom equivalence, then injectivity of the localized extension-adjunction Hom equivalence, and evaluate on slice sections. The concrete integral forward-functor equality lets every transported slice section be written in terms of an original section. Naturality of both scalar units and both localized extension units therefore proves naturality of the constructed finite isomorphisms from their generator formula. The same test proves equality of any two normalized comparison components, hence equality of natural isomorphisms and TensorComparison structures. Assemble the independent finite levels to obtain unique existence.
